notes: Same B-GLS CONSTANT model as WA and ID. Its 290 streamgages include Oregon coastal, Columbia, Klamath (e.g. 11502500) and Great Basin (e.g. 10396000) sites (Table B1; Figure B1 p. 49), but SIR 2016-5118 pp. 1, 23 define the study region as the Columbia basin, the OR/WA coast and the rest of WA, which leaves out the Oregon closed basins (HUC 1712) and the Klamath (1801). regional_skew_at/regional_skew_at_huc therefore treat those two as unresolved and raise (regional_skew_hucs.csv); this state-keyed row is the deliberate way to apply the study there. Cross-checked against SIR 2016-5118 Table A2 p. 66. No Oregon-specific report has adopted it yet: Cooper (2005, SIR 2005-5116) predates B-GLS.

table: Table B2 (p. 53); text p. 52 (G = -0.07, AVPnew = MSE = 0.18, effective record length 41 yr)
notes: B-GLS CONSTANT model; AVPnew 0.18 is the B17 MSE (SE 0.4243), 2.4 times the information content of the B17B map (p. 52). NOT valid in the Snake River Plain (regression region 0): see the separate ID Snake River Plain row. Cross-checked against SIR 2016-5118 Table A2 p. 66.

No regional skew exists here. SIR 2016-5083 p. 52: the PNW regional skew model is not valid in the Snake River Plain (region 0 in figure 3) because of extensive regulation, localized groundwater-surface water interactions and substantial infiltration, and should not be used to estimate a weighted skew there.

Not representable as one value. Siefken, S.A., Williams-Sether, T., Barth, N.A., Chase, K.J., and Cedar Face, M.A., 2025, SIR 2025-5019, pp. 9-10 (https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20255019): no B-WLS/B-GLS regional skew study covers any part of MT/ND/SD/WY; USGS MT practice uses the spatially varying B17B Plate I map (not recommended by B17C p. 31, and never a silent fallback here) with SE 0.55. Parrett and Johnson (2004, WRI 03-4308) found SE 0.64 for MT gages, which is what vendor/peakfqr/inst/testdata/wymt_ffa_2022A.psf uses with per-station GenSkew from -0.0053 to -0.4. The PNW B-GLS study (SIR 2016-5083 app. B, G = -0.07, MSE 0.18) does cover western MT: SIR 2016-5118 pp. 1 and 23 define its region as the Columbia River Basin south of the U.S.-Canada border, and all 23 MT gages it used are in HUC 1701 (Kootenai, Clark Fork, Blackfoot, Bitterroot, Flathead). But USGS MT deliberately does not use it: SIR 2018-5046 pp. 20-21 keeps the Plate I map statewide for consistency (SE 0.64), and SIR 2025-5019 (SE 0.55, its data-release psf included) applies the map to western-MT Columbia gages too. Left pending per B17C ('consult with the USGS'); a western-MT PNW row would diverge from current USGS MT practice. The vendored psf's SE 0.64 predates the 0.55 guidance. Location lookups (regional_skew_at, regional_skew_at_huc, regional_skew_for_site) follow the study's own region, so a western-MT site in HUC 1701 gets the PNW value with RegionalSkew.advisory set and a logged warning; east of the Divide (Missouri, HUC 10; St. Mary/Belly, HUC 09) they raise.

The verified PNW value (G = -0.07, MSE 0.18), extended to Oregon's closed basins (HUC4 1712), which SIR 2016-5118 pp. 1, 23 leave out of the study region although 4 study gages are there. A CONSTANT B-GLS fit to the 8 screened Oregon gages in 1712 (pre-regulation records of at least 25 peaks; GAGES-II regulated/urban without a coded start out; nested pairs out) gives G = -0.19 (SD 0.21), t = -0.59 against -0.07: consistent, but with that SD the test cannot detect differences smaller than about 0.4. Returned only with allow_provisional=True. The Klamath (1801) stays unresolved: 2 screened gages.

CONSTANT B-GLS model, 240 gages east of the Continental Divide (Missouri and Hudson Bay drainages in MT, plus WY/ID gages in the shared HUC4s 1002, 1007, 1008), water years through 2025: G = -0.04 (SD 0.09), MSE (AVPnew) 0.385, effective record length 22 yr. That MSE is LARGER than the 0.302 Bulletin 17B gives its Plate I map, which USGS Montana applies statewide with SE 0.55 (SIR 2025-5019 pp. 9-10): this value carries less information than current USGS practice and earns little weight. Mean annual precipitation is significant (G = -0.694 + 0.342 PRECIP/10, PRECIP in inches, MSE 0.335; t = 5.0), but a covariate model is not representable here; see the doc. West of the Divide (HUC 1701) the verified Pacific Northwest study applies. A published USGS study supersedes this.

notes: B-WLS/B-GLS CONSTANT model fit to 307 streamgages in Arizona and the surrounding states (app. 1, p. 49); no basin characteristic gave a pseudo-R2 above 10 percent (p. 52). The abstract (p. 1) calls it a statewide regional skew, so regional_skew_hucs.csv makes every HUC8 touching Arizona a member valid in AZ only: a site in a HUC8 shared with NM, UT, NV, CA, CO or Mexico needs its state. Table 1-2 prints b1 = -0.09 (SD 0.06), model error variance 0.08 (SD 0.02), ASEV 0.003, AVPnew 0.08, pseudo-R2 0. SE = sqrt(0.08) = 0.2828. Supersedes WSP 2433's constant skew of 0 with MSE 0.31 (pp. 1, 3). The report's flood frequency used PeakfqSA 0.974 (p. 16). Cross-checked: abstract p. 1, p. 54 text, Table 1-2 p. 55 and the summary p. 42 agree.

No verified regional skew for New Mexico. Current USGS NM practice, Waltemeyer (2008, SIR 2008-5119, p. 5; the report NM.json and NM StreamStats use), sets the generalized skew to zero with MSE 0.31 for all nine flood regions, taken from Thomas and others (1997, WSP 2433): a Bulletin 17B-era value, not a B-WLS/B-GLS study. Its successor, Tillery, Bell and Wagner (2026, 'Regression equations for the estimation of the magnitude and frequency of floods at ungaged locations on unregulated streams in New Mexico'), computed an updated regional skew of -0.145 (SE 0.454, MSE 0.206) from 346 gages in NM and parts of AZ, CO, OK, TX and UT through WY2020 (data release https://doi.org/10.5066/P9QWEXCY, abstract). As of 2026-10-12 that report is not in the USGS Publications Warehouse, and the data release was withdrawn on 2026-09-29 ('currently being revised and is temporarily unavailable'), so neither the value's method nor its region can be checked. Left pending; transcribe from the published report.

No B-WLS/B-GLS regional skew study covers Colorado. Both current USGS Colorado peak-flow reports weight station skews with the Bulletin 17B Plate I map: Kohn, Mast and Gross (2026, SIR 2025-5047, central and western Colorado, data through WY2019, https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20255047) p. 7 ('the national regionalized skew map (plate I, IACWD, 1982) based on streamgage data through water year 1973, which is the most current (2024) regional skew map in Colorado'), and Kohn and others (2016, SIR 2016-5099, eastern Colorado, https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20165099) p. 19 (the same map, 'the most current skew map in Colorado'). B17C p. 31 does not recommend the Plate I map, and flowfreq never applies it silently. Left pending per B17C ('consult with the USGS'). Checked 2026-10-12.

No B-WLS/B-GLS regional skew study covers Utah. Kenney, Wilkowske and Wright (2007, SIR 2007-5158 ver. 4.0, https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20075158) p. 6 and fig. 4 (p. 7) weight station skews with the generalized skew contour map of Perica and Stayner (2004), drawn by interpolating the skews of stations with at least 30 years of record; the report gives no mean square error for it, and it is not a Bayesian regression. That report is still the one UT.json and NSS use. Tillery and others (2026; New Mexico, skew -0.145) included some Utah gages but is a New Mexico study, unpublished as of 2026-10-12 (see the NM row). Left pending per B17C p. 31. Checked 2026-10-12.

No B-WLS/B-GLS regional skew study covers Wyoming. Siefken and others (2025, SIR 2025-5019, pp. 9-10, https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20255019), the current USGS peak-flow frequency methods for MT, ND, SD and WY, applies the Bulletin 17B Plate I map with SE 0.55, as for Montana (see the MT row). Miller (2003, WRIR 03-4107), the report WY.json uses for its equations, predates B17C. The provisional Montana study (allow_provisional=True) used 20 WY gages but its row is valid in MT only. Left pending per B17C p. 31. Checked 2026-10-12.

No B-WLS/B-GLS regional skew study covers Nevada. Thomas, Hjalmarson and Waltemeyer (1997, WSP 2433, https://doi.org/10.3133/wsp2433), still the only report NV.json and NSS use, found no regional pattern among 1,042 adjusted station skews in the southwestern United States and used a regional skew of zero with error equal to the sample variance, 0.31 (abstract p. 1; 'Regional Skew Coefficient', pp. 74-79): a Bulletin 17B-era value. For Arizona that value was superseded by SIR 2014-5211's B-GLS study (see the AZ row), which does not extend into Nevada. Left pending per B17C p. 31. Checked 2026-10-12.
